note: Seeded from model knowledge; clearance figures are the manufacturer-published maxima where recalled confidently, null otherwise.

records.name: North
records.notes: Walnut slat front with a mesh layer behind it; ships with two 140mm Aspect intake fans. A mesh side panel version exists alongside the tempered glass one and breathes noticeably better with a hot GPU. GPU figure is the published maximum with a front fan installed.

records.name: North XL
records.notes: Taller, deeper North with more radiator and drive capacity. Clearance figures and included fan count not recalled with confidence, so left null rather than borrowed from the standard North.

records.name: Meshify 2
records.notes: Mesh-front sibling of the Define 7 sharing the same chassis and open/storage layout switch. GPU figure is the published length with a front fan fitted; the open layout with the front fan removed clears substantially more, but that larger number is not recalled precisely.

records.name: Meshify 2 Compact
records.notes: Smaller Meshify 2 without the storage layout. Clearances nulled: my recall conflicts with the full-size Meshify 2 numbers and I will not guess between them.

records.name: Meshify C
records.notes: The case that started the mesh-front trend; still very common second-hand. Ships with two 120mm Dynamic X2 GP-12 fans. Cooler clearance nulled — I recall competing 170mm and 172mm figures for the Define C / Meshify C chassis.

records.name: Define 7
records.notes: Sound-dampened solid front with side intake channels; same chassis as the Meshify 2. Quiet by design, and correspondingly airflow-limited compared with its mesh twin. GPU figure is with a front fan fitted.

records.name: Define R5
records.notes: The classic silent build case, everywhere on the second-hand market. GPU figure is the published maximum with the middle drive cage removed; with the cage in place it is far shorter. Ships with two 140mm Dynamic GP-14 fans.

records.name: Pop Air
records.notes: Budget-tier mesh front, three 120mm Aspect fans included. Clearance figures not recalled confidently.

records.name: Torrent
records.notes: Airflow-first design: two 180mm front fans plus three 140mm in the floor, five fans in total, and no 5.25in or front drive obstruction. One of the coolest-running ATX cases available; the trade-off is bulk and fan noise at load.

records.name: Terra
records.notes: Roughly 10L wood-and-aluminium Mini-ITX sandwich case with a repositionable central spine that trades CPU cooler height against GPU thickness. SFX/SFX-L power supply only. Clearances are configuration-dependent and not recalled precisely, so nulled.

records.name: Focus G
records.notes: Cheap ATX tower with mesh side intakes on the front panel; a very common first-build and second-hand chassis. Included fan count varies by colour/LED SKU, so nulled.

records.name: O11 Dynamic
records.notes: Dual-chamber showcase case designed with Der8auer. Ships with NO fans — thermals depend entirely on what the owner fits. With side and bottom intake populated it cools well; run bare it is poor, so treat the airflow tier as potential rather than out-of-box.

records.name: O11 Dynamic EVO
records.notes: Reworked O11 with reversible layout and modular front I/O. Also ships without fans. Clearance figures nulled — I could not separate them cleanly from the original O11 Dynamic.

records.name: O11 Air Mini
records.notes: Mesh-panelled compact version of the O11 that, unlike the Dynamic, ships with fans. Takes ATX boards despite the small footprint.

records.name: Lancool 215
records.notes: Budget airflow standout: two 200mm ARGB front intakes plus a 120mm rear exhaust. Large slow fans mean strong cooling at low noise.

records.name: Lancool II Mesh
records.notes: Mesh-front revision of the Lancool II with hinged side panels. Included fan count differs between the plain, RGB and Performance SKUs, so nulled.

records.name: Lancool III
records.notes: Large mesh tower shipping with four 140mm PWM fans and very generous radiator support. Clearances not recalled precisely.

records.name: H510
records.notes: Extremely popular and thermally poor: solid front panel with only a thin side intake gap, and no top radiator mount. Quiet because airflow is choked, not because it is well damped. Ships with two 120mm Aer F fans.

records.name: H5 Flow
records.notes: The corrective to the H510: perforated front and a floor intake position under the GPU. Clearances nulled.

records.name: H7 Flow
records.notes: Full mesh front and top, three included fans, and proper 360mm support in both positions.

records.name: H210
records.notes: Mini-ITX version of the H510 and it inherits the same choked front panel. Surprisingly long GPU clearance for the footprint.

records.name: S340
records.notes: The pre-H-series budget favourite; large numbers still in circulation second-hand. Clearances nulled.

records.name: 4000D Airflow
records.notes: The default mid-range recommendation for several years. Two 120mm AirGuide fans included, which is on the light side for the mesh front — a third intake helps materially.

records.name: iCUE 4000X RGB
records.notes: Same chassis as the 4000D but with a tempered glass front, so intake is via the side gaps only. Ships with three SP120 RGB Elite fans, which partly offsets the restriction.

records.name: 5000D Airflow
records.notes: Larger 4000D with a side radiator mount and much better cable management space. Also only two fans included.

records.name: 7000D Airflow
records.notes: Full tower with mesh front, huge radiator capacity and three 140mm fans included. Clearance figures nulled — I could not separate them reliably from the 5000D.

records.name: Carbide 275R
records.notes: Plain, cheap, solid-front ATX tower that sold in volume; a later 275R Airflow SKU swapped in a mesh front and breathes better. This record describes the original solid-front version.

records.name: Eclipse P400A
records.notes: Ultra-fine mesh front that measured near the top of its class on release, with three 120mm D-RGB fans included on the Digital SKU. The plain P400A ships with fewer fans.

records.name: Eclipse G360A
records.notes: Budget mesh tower with three included D-RGB 120mm intakes. Clearances not recalled confidently.

records.name: Eclipse P500A
records.notes: Larger mesh Phanteks with 140mm-class front mounts and very high radiator ceiling. Included fan count differs between the plain and D-RGB SKUs, so nulled.

records.name: Pure Base 500DX
records.notes: Mesh front and top with three Pure Wings 2 140mm fans included — the airflow version of be quiet!'s usual silence-first formula. Unusually generous CPU cooler clearance for the size.

records.name: Pure Base 600
records.notes: Damped solid front with bottom intake slots. Quiet, mid-pack thermals. Clearances nulled.

records.name: Silent Base 802
records.notes: Ships with interchangeable solid (damped) and mesh front/top panels, so the owner picks the silence/airflow point. Tiers here describe the damped configuration it ships assembled in.

records.name: NR200P
records.notes: The mainstream Mini-ITX case: roughly 18L, mesh on nearly every surface, SFX/SFX-L power supply. Cooler clearance is 155mm with the vented side panel and far lower (about 76mm) if the tempered glass panel is fitted — the 155mm figure is the mesh configuration. Included fan count nulled; it differs across NR200 and NR200P/NR200P MAX SKUs.

records.name: TD500 Mesh
records.notes: Crystalline mesh front with three ARGB 120mm intakes included; a common budget airflow pick. Clearances nulled.

records.name: MasterBox NR600
records.notes: Plain mesh-front ATX tower, sold with and without an ODD bay. Clearances nulled.

records.name: MasterBox Q300L
records.notes: Very cheap Micro-ATX cube with magnetic dust filter panels and a single 120mm rear exhaust included. Front intake depends on which perforated panel arrangement the owner uses.

records.name: HAF 912
records.notes: High Air Flow era budget tower — 200mm front intake and 120mm rear exhaust, thin steel, no dampening. Still turns up constantly in cheap second-hand builds.

records.name: Y60
records.notes: Three-sided glass fishbowl with an included vertical GPU riser. Intake is bottom and side only, so it runs warmer than a mesh case despite three included fans.

records.name: Y70
records.notes: Larger Y60 successor, also glass-fronted with a vertical GPU mount; a Touch variant adds a display panel. Included fan count and clearances not recalled confidently.

records.name: M1
records.notes: Roughly 12.7L aluminium Mini-ITX classic, revised repeatedly (v5, v6, v6.1) with different GPU thickness and radiator options per revision — releaseYear is the original crowdfunded launch. Ships bare, no fans. GPU length nulled because it changed across revisions.

records.name: Meshlicious
records.notes: Full-mesh sandwich-layout Mini-ITX case at roughly 15L, supporting full-length triple-slot GPUs via a riser. No fans included. Clearances are layout-dependent and nulled.

records.name: AIR 903 MAX
records.notes: Cheap mesh tower whose selling point is four 140mm ARGB fans in the box. Clearances not recalled confidently.

records.name: CH510
records.notes: Budget mesh-front tower with a single pre-installed 120mm rear exhaust — front intakes must be bought separately, which materially changes its thermals.

records.name: DF700 Flux
records.notes: Five fans included, including a small PSU-shroud fan blowing up onto the graphics card — the "Flux" platform feature. Good value cooling, unremarkable build quality.

records.name: Versa H18
records.notes: Bottom-tier Micro-ATX tower with a solid plastic front and narrow side intake slits, one 120mm rear fan. Common in cheap prebuilts and first builds; expect high component temperatures unless fans are added.

records.name: OptiPlex 7010 SFF
records.notes: Ex-office desktop, ubiquitous and cheap second-hand. Takes half-height, low-profile cards only and uses a proprietary low-wattage TFX power supply with non-standard connectors, so a normal GPU upgrade is not possible without swapping the chassis. Clearances nulled: the constraint is card height and PSU wattage, not a published millimetre maximum.

records.name: EliteDesk 800 G4 SFF
records.fullName: HP EliteDesk 800 G4 Small Form Factor
records.notes: Same story as the OptiPlex: low-profile half-height GPUs only, proprietary PSU and front-panel wiring. Near-silent at idle, ramps hard and audibly under sustained load, which is why the noise tier is moderate rather than quiet.
